spec_notes: ratchet/spec.md marks many of these choices as Open for the requester (C-19 token precedence and refused env token, C-23 bot names, C-26 conversation labels, C-27/C-28 empty conversations and restore, C-37 sends while pending, C-40 automatic retry, C-43/C-46/C-47/C-49/C-51 name collisions, renaming in Edit and edits to an applied instruction, C-65 eligible fields, C-66 id preview, C-67/C-76 proposal lifetime, C-77 stale proposals, C-79 next free, C-82 Tasks scope, C-83/C-96 resume versus Interrupted, C-87 away report, C-88/C-89 steering, C-91 in-flight cancel, C-100 narrow widths), yet the product then decides every one of them (environment token wins, duplicate names refused, 80-character limit, first-message titles cut at 45 characters, copy-on-Use, Interrupted plus manual Retry, report kept until Mark as reviewed, and so on) and the spec never records those decisions; they appear only in the README. Discovery clauses C-105 to C-116 decide behaviour in ordinary requirement lines (storage recovery, memory precedence, focus after decisions, replay of one submission, token-like field values) without marking them as the builder's choices. The spec does not contradict the request on my items. It is silent on how a non-matching forget is reported, on capitalised field names, on identifiers such as ORD-1001A and on logging of server errors.
tests_notes: One file, test/rules.test.js, with 13 long scenario tests, each checking many behaviours (for example "setup, person selection, workspace scope and saved material survive a restart" covers setup, bot naming, instructions, saved tasks, memory, person isolation and restart together), so a failure names a scenario, not a rule. Several tests are tied to internals: they open app/store.js directly, mock fs.renameSync on the exact path DATA_DIR/state.json, read state.json and assert its internal shape (tasks[0].claim.index, attempts [1,1,1], events), assert validator path strings such as workspaces[0].tasks and proposals[0].origin, and depend on the /api/action contract (person field, request ids, the turn notice field, report.end boundaries). Timing is pinned through STANDIN_STEP_MS=70, STANDIN_SLOW_MS=100 and fixed pauses (pause(700)). Another correct build with a different storage layout, API or wording would fail most of them. Nothing tests the page itself (names, focus, narrow layout, conversation labels, bot-name length), the non-matching forget, capitalised fields, unknown ids like ORD-1001A, or server error logging.
maintainer: app/snapshot.js validates every cross-reference of the whole saved state at startup (turn order, claims, attempts against results, event streams against task results, proposal origins), and there is no migration, so any new field or changed shape must be mirrored there exactly, or existing data folders stop starting. The browser code in public/app.js re-renders by string patching on a 325 ms poll with hand-written focus restoration, draft and submission tracking, and away-report boundaries kept in sessionStorage; small markup changes can break focus or replay protection without any test noticing.
